questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, how many maxima can be seen on a screen (including central maxima) if d = $\dfrac{5\lambda}{2}$ (where λ is wavelength of light and d is distance between the two slits).
questions.explanation: Maxima occur when $d\sin\theta=n\lambda$, i.e., $n\le d/\lambda=2.5$. So n = 0, ±1, ±2, giving 5 maxima in total.

questions.q: If AB is incident plane wave front then refracted wave front is ($n_2 > n_1$) [figure: plane wavefront AB entering a converging lens from medium $n_1$ into $n_2$]
options: a smoothly curving concave wavefront, more curved (option 2)
questions.explanation: Passing into the denser medium via the lens, the central part of the wavefront (thicker glass) is delayed more than the edges, bending the initially plane wavefront into a converging spherical (concave) wavefront, as in option 2.

questions.q: The total energy carried by the light wave when it travels from a rarer to a non-reflecting and non-absorbing medium
options: either increases or decreases depending upon angle of incidence
questions.explanation: If the medium reflects nothing and absorbs nothing, all the incident energy is transmitted, so the total energy carried by the wave remains the same.

questions.q: Three polaroid sheets are co-axially placed as indicated in the diagram. Pass axes of the polaroids 2 and 3 make $30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ with pass axis of polaroid sheet 1. If $I_0$ is the intensity of the incident unpolarised light entering sheet 1, the intensity of the emergent light through sheet 3 is [unpolarised light $I_0$ passes through polaroid 1, then polaroid 2 at $30^\circ$ to polaroid 1's pass axis, then polaroid 3 at $90^\circ$ to polaroid 1's pass axis]
questions.explanation: Intensity after sheet 1 is $I_0/2$; applying Malus's law through sheets 2 and 3 (at $30^\circ$ and then $60^\circ$) gives $I=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^230^\circ\sin^230^\circ=\dfrac{3I_0}{32}$.

questions.q: When light propagates through a given homogeneous medium, the velocities of
options: primary wavefronts are lesser than those of secondary wavelets.
primary wavefronts are greater than or equal to those of secondary wavelets.
primary wavefront and wavelets are equal.
primary wavefront are larger than those of secondary wavelets.
questions.explanation: In a homogeneous medium the speed of light is the same everywhere, so the primary wavefront and Huygens' secondary wavelets travel with equal speed.

questions.q: An unpolarised light of intensity I is passed through two polaroids kept one after the other with their planes parallel to each other. The intensity of light emerging from second polaroid is $\dfrac{I}{4}$. The angle between the pass axes of the polaroids is
questions.explanation: The first polaroid halves the intensity to I/2; applying Malus's law, (I/2)cos²θ = I/4 gives cos²θ = 1/2, so θ = 45°.

questions.q: In the Young's double slit experiment, the intensity of light passing through each of the two double slits is 2 × 10$^{-2}$ Wm$^{-2}$. The screen-slit distance is very large in comparison with slit-slit distance. The fringe width is $\beta$. The distance between the central maximum and a point P on the screen is $x=\dfrac{\beta}{3}$. Then the total light intensity at that point is
questions.explanation: Path difference x=β/3 corresponds to phase $\delta=2\pi/3$. I = 4I$_0$cos²(δ/2) = 4×2×10$^{-2}$×cos²(60°) = 4×2×10$^{-2}\times0.25$ = 2×10$^{-2}$ Wm$^{-2}$.

questions.q: In case of Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit, the diffraction pattern on the screen is described correctly by which of the following statements?
options: Central dark band having uniform brightness on either side.
Central dark band having alternate dark and bright bands of decreasing intensity on either side.
Central bright band having dark bands on either side.
Central bright band having alternate dark and bright bands of decreasing intensity on either side.
questions.explanation: In single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction the central maximum is bright and most intense; on either side there are alternately dark and bright fringes of steadily decreasing intensity.

questions.q: When a Compact Disc (CD) is illuminated by a small source of white light, coloured bands are observed. This is due to
questions.explanation: The closely spaced tracks on a CD act like a reflection diffraction grating; different wavelengths diffract at different angles, producing the coloured bands.

questions.q: For light diverging from a finite point source
options: the intensity at the wave front does not depend on the distance.
the intensity decreases in proportion to the distance squared.
questions.explanation: A point source emits spherical wavefronts; the same power spreads over a sphere of area $4\pi r^2$, so the intensity falls off as $1/r^2$, i.e. in proportion to the square of the distance.

questions.q: The fringe width for red colour as compared to that for violet colour is approximately
questions.explanation: Fringe width $\beta \propto \lambda$. Since $\lambda_{red}$ ($\approx$700 nm) is roughly double $\lambda_{violet}$ ($\approx$400 nm), the fringe width for red light is approximately double that for violet.

questions.q: A slit of width 'a' is illuminated by red light of wavelength 6500A°. If the first diffraction minimum falls at 30°, then the value of 'a' is _____
questions.explanation: First minimum: $a\sin\theta=\lambda\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{6500\times10^{-10}}{\sin30^\circ}=1.3\times10^{-6}$ m $=1.3$ micron.

questions.q: Which of the statements are correct with reference to single slit diffraction pattern? (i) Fringes are of unequal width (ii) Fringes are of equal width (iii) Light energy is conserved (iv) Intensities of all bright fringes are equal
questions.explanation: In single-slit diffraction, fringe widths are unequal (central maximum is widest) and light energy is conserved (redistributed, not lost) — (i) and (iii) are correct.

questions.q: In the Young's double slit experiment a monochromatic source of wavelength $\lambda$ is used. The intensity of light passing through each slit is I$_0$. The intensity of light reaching the screen S$_c$ at a point P, a distance x from O is given by (Take d << D).
questions.explanation: Path difference $=\dfrac{dx}{D}$, phase $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi dx}{\lambda D}$; intensity $I=4I_0\cos^2(\phi/2)=4I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi dx}{\lambda D}\right)$.

questions.q: Three polaroid sheets P$_1$, P$_2$ and P$_3$ are kept parallel to each other such that the angle between the pass axes of P$_1$ and P$_2$ is $45^\circ$ and that between P$_2$ and P$_3$ is $45^\circ$. If unpolarised beam of light of intensity 128 Wm$^{-2}$ is incident on P$_1$, what is the intensity of light coming out of P$_3$?
Two poles are separated by a distance of 3.14 m. The resolving power of human eye is 1 minute of an arc. The maximum distance from which he can identify the two poles distinctly is
questions.explanation: Resolving angle $\theta=1'=2.91\times10^{-4}$ rad; distance $=\dfrac{\text{separation}}{\theta}=\dfrac{3.14}{2.91\times10^{-4}}\approx10.8$ km.

questions.q: In Young's Double Slit Experiment, the distance between the slits and the screen is 1.2 m and the distance between the two slits is 2.4 mm. If a thin transparent mica sheet of thickness 1 $\mu$m and R.I. 1.5 is introduced between one of the interfering beams, the shift in the position of the central bright fringe is

[Graph shows sin r (y-axis) versus sin i (x-axis) as a straight line through the origin making an angle of 30$^\circ$ with the sin i axis] A transparent medium shows relation between i and r as shown. If the speed of light in vacuum is c the Brewster angle for the medium is
questions.explanation: The graph slope gives $\sin r/\sin i = \tan30^\circ$, so refractive index $n = \sin i/\sin r = \cot30^\circ = \sqrt3$; Brewster's angle satisfies $\tan i_p = n = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow i_p = 60^\circ$.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, the intensity of light at a point on the screen where path difference is $\lambda$ is K units. The intensity of light at a point where path difference is $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$ is
questions.explanation: $I = 4I_0\cos^2(\phi/2)$; at path difference $\lambda$, $\phi=2\pi$ gives $I=4I_0=K$; at path difference $\lambda/3$, $\phi = 2\pi/3$ gives $I = 4I_0\cos^2(\pi/3) = 4I_0(1/4) = I_0 = K/4$.

questions.q: Due to Doppler's effect the shift in wavelength observed is 0.1 Å for a star producing wavelength 6000 Å. Velocity of recession of the star will be
questions.explanation: For the Doppler effect of light, $v = c\dfrac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda} = 3\times10^5 \times \dfrac{0.1}{6000} = 5$ km/s.

questions.q: A plane wavefront of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a single slit of width a. The angular width of principal maximum is
questions.explanation: The central maximum in single-slit diffraction extends between the first minima on either side, at angles ±$\lambda$/a, giving a total angular width of 2$\lambda$/a.

questions.q: In a Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit, if yellow light illuminating the slit is replaced by blue light, then diffraction bands
questions.explanation: Fringe/band width in diffraction is proportional to wavelength; since blue light has a shorter wavelength than yellow, the diffraction bands become narrower.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, two wavelengths $\lambda_1$ = 780 nm and $\lambda_2$ = 520 nm are used to obtain interference fringes. If the n$^{th}$ bright band due to $\lambda_1$ coincides with (n + 1)$^{th}$ bright band due to $\lambda_2$, then the value of n is

In Young's double slit experiment, slits are separated by 2 mm and the screen is placed at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits. Light consisting of two wavelengths 6500 Å and 5200 Å are used to obtain interference fringes. Then the separation between the fourth bright fringes of two different patterns produced by the two wavelengths is
questions.explanation: Position of the 4th bright fringe is y = 4$\lambda$D/d. Separation = 4D($\lambda_1$−$\lambda_2$)/d = 4(1.2)(1300×10$^{-10}$)/(2×10$^{-3}$) ≈ 0.312 mm.

questions.q: During scattering of light, the amount of scattering is inversely proportional to ________ of wavelength of light.
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh's scattering law, the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength, $I \propto 1/\lambda^4$.

questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment if yellow light is replaced by blue light, the interference fringes become
questions.explanation: Fringe width $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than yellow, so the fringes become narrower.

questions.q: According to Huygens' principle, during refraction of light from air to a denser medium
questions.explanation: On entering a denser medium, the speed of light decreases; since frequency stays constant, $\lambda=v/f$ shows wavelength also decreases.

questions.q: In a system of two crossed polarisers, it is found that the intensity of light from the second polariser is half from that of first polariser. The angle between their pass axes is
questions.explanation: By Malus's law, $I=I_0\cos^2\theta$. Given $I=I_0/2$, $\cos^2\theta=1/2 \Rightarrow \theta=45°$.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment the source is white light. One slit is covered with red filter and the other with blue filter. There shall be
questions.explanation: Since the two slits now emit light of different wavelengths (colours), they are not coherent with a fixed phase relation for interference, so no stationary interference fringe pattern is observed.

questions.q: Light of wavelength 600 nm is incident normally on a slit of width 0.2 mm. The angular width of central maxima in the diffraction pattern is (measured from minimum to minimum)
questions.explanation: Angular width (min to min) $=\dfrac{2\lambda}{a}=\dfrac{2\times600\times10^{-9}}{0.2\times10^{-3}}=6\times10^{-3}$ rad.

questions.q: For what distance is ray optics a good approximation when the aperture is 4 mm and the wavelength of light is 400 nm ?
questions.explanation: Ray optics is a good approximation up to the Fresnel distance $z_F=\dfrac{a^2}{\lambda}=\dfrac{(4\times10^{-3})^2}{400\times10^{-9}}=40$ m; the KEA key credited all four options (grace mark for everyone).

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment the slit separation is 0.5 m from the slits. For a monochromatic light of wavelength 500 nm, the distance of 3rd maxima from 2nd minima on the other side is
questions.explanation: The printed data is inconsistent (a 'slit separation' cannot be 'from the slits'). Assuming the intended values were slit separation d=1 mm and screen distance D=1 m: fringe width $\lambda D/d=0.5$ mm; distance of 3rd maxima from 2nd minima on the other side $=(3+1.5)\times0.5=2.25$ mm, matching option (4). KEA likely awarded a grace mark to everyone owing to this ambiguity in the printed question (as per KEA key).

questions.q: To observe diffraction, the size of the obstacle
options: should be $\lambda/2$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength.
should be much larger than the wavelength.
should be of the order of wavelength.
questions.explanation: Noticeable diffraction occurs when the obstacle/aperture size is comparable to (of the order of) the wavelength of the wave.

questions.q: The polarizing angle of glass is 57°. A ray of light which is incident at this angle will have an angle of refraction as
questions.explanation: At Brewster's (polarizing) angle, the refracted and reflected rays are perpendicular, so the angle of refraction = 90° − 57° = 33°.

questions.q: A fringe width of a certain interference pattern is $\beta$ = 0.002 cm. What is the distance of 5$^{th}$ dark fringe from centre?
questions.explanation: Using y = n$\beta$ = 5 \times 0.002 = 0.01 cm = 1\times10^{-2} cm (option 3); the stricter formula y=(n-1/2)$\beta$ gives 0.009 cm — this ambiguity is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: A polarized light of intensity I$_0$ is passed through another polarizer whose pass axis makes an angle of 60$^{\circ}$ with the pass axis of the former. What is the intensity of emergent polarized light from second polarizer?

Which of the following phenomena support the wave theory of light ?
(a) scattering
(b) interference
(c) diffraction
(d) velocity of light in a denser medium is less than the velocity of light in the rarer medium
questions.explanation: Interference and diffraction are explained only by wave theory. The lower speed of light in a denser medium (predicted by Huygens' wave theory, contrary to Newton's corpuscular theory) also supports the wave nature; scattering does not specifically favour either theory.

questions.q: White light reflected from a soap film (Refractive Index = 1.5) has a maxima at 600 nm and a minima at 450 nm with no minimum in between. Then the thickness of the film is ______ $\times$ 10$^{-7}$ m.
questions.explanation: For reflected light: minima $2\mu t=m\lambda$, maxima $2\mu t=(n+\tfrac12)\lambda$. Taking the adjacent orders $m=2$ (for 450 nm) and $n=1$ (for 600 nm) gives $2\mu t=900$ nm, so $t=900/(2\times1.5)=300$ nm $=3\times10^{-7}$ m.

questions.q: A cylindrical tube of length 0.2 m and radius R with sugar solution of concentration 'C' produce a rotation of $\theta$ in the plane of vibration of a plane polarized light. The same sugar solution is transferred to another tube of length 0.3 m of same radius. The remaining gap is filled by distilled water. Now the optical rotation produced is
questions.explanation: Optical rotation $\theta\propto$ concentration $\times$ length. Spreading the same amount of sugar over a longer tube (0.3 m instead of 0.2 m, same radius) reduces its concentration to $\dfrac{0.2}{0.3}C=\dfrac23C$, so the new rotation $=k\times\dfrac23C\times0.3=k\times C\times0.2=\theta$, unchanged.

questions.q: A monochromatic beam of light is travelling from medium A of refractive index n$_1$ to medium B of refractive index n$_2$. In the medium A, there are x number of waves in a certain distance. In the medium B, there are y number of waves in the same distance. Then, refractive index of medium A with respect to medium B is....
questions.explanation: Wavelength in A is (distance)/x and in B is (distance)/y; since $_An_B = v_B/v_A = \lambda_B/\lambda_A$ (same frequency), $_An_B$ = x/y.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, fringes of width $\beta$ are produced on a screen kept at a distance of 1 m from the slit. When the screen is moved away by 5$\times$10$^{-2}$ m, fringe width changes by 3$\times$10$^{-5}$ m. The separation between the slits is 1$\times$10$^{-3}$ m. The wavelength of the light used is ......... nm.
questions.explanation: $\beta = \lambda D/d$, so $\lambda = (\Delta\beta \cdot d)/\Delta D = (3\times10^{-5}\times10^{-3})/(5\times10^{-2}) = 6\times10^{-7}$ m = 600 nm.

questions.q: For sustained interference fringes in double slit experiment, essential condition/s is/are (a) sources must be coherent (b) the intensities of the two sources must be equal. Here, the correct option/s is/are
questions.explanation: Coherence of the two sources is essential for a sustained interference pattern; equal intensity is not necessary, it only affects the contrast of the fringes.

questions.q: In single slit experiment, the width of the slit is reduced. Then, the linear width of the principal maxima..........
questions.explanation: The angular width of the central maximum is proportional to 1/a, so it increases as the slit width a decreases; but less light passes through the narrower slit, so it becomes less bright.

questions.q: If the two slits in Young's double slit experiment are of unequal width, then
options: the bright fringes will have unequal spacing.
the bright fringes will have unequal brightness.
the dark fringes are not perfectly dark.
questions.explanation: Unequal slit widths give unequal intensities I$_1$ $\ne$ I$_2$ from the two slits; the fringe spacing and bright-fringe intensity are unaffected, but the minimum intensity $(\sqrt{I_1}-\sqrt{I_2})^2\ne0$, so the dark fringes are not perfectly dark.

questions.q: The phenomenon of polarization shows that light has _________ nature.
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized, so polarization confirms that light is a transverse wave.

questions.q: Wavefront is the locus of all points, where the particles of the medium vibrate with the same .................
questions.explanation: By definition, a wavefront is the locus of points in a medium vibrating in the same phase.

questions.q: Two monochromatic light waves of amplitudes $3A$ and $2A$ interfering at a point have a phase difference of $60^0$. The intensity at that point will be proportional to .................
questions.explanation: Resultant intensity $\propto A_1^2+A_2^2+2A_1A_2\cos\phi = 9A^2+4A^2+2(3A)(2A)\cos60^0 = 13A^2+6A^2=19A^2$.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in case of Young's double slit experiment. a) A slit $S$ is necessary if we use an ordinary extended source of light. b) A slit $S$ is not needed if we use an ordinary but well collimated beam of light. c) A slit $S$ is not needed if we use a spatially coherent source of light. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A single slit $S$ is used to obtain spatial coherence from an extended incoherent source; it is unnecessary when the source is already collimated or spatially coherent, so all three statements a), b) and c) are correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: A parallel beam of light of wavelength 6000 Å gets diffracted by a single slit of width 0.3 mm. The angular position of the first minima of diffracted light is ...........
questions.explanation: First minima at $\theta=\lambda/a = (6\times10^{-7})/(3\times10^{-4}) = 2\times10^{-3}$ rad.

questions.q: The critical angle of a certain medium is $Sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)$. The polarizing angle of the medium is .............
questions.explanation: $\sin C=3/5 \Rightarrow \mu=1/\sin C=5/3$; Brewster's angle $\theta_p=Tan^{-1}\mu=Tan^{-1}(5/3)$.

questions.q: A boat has green light of wavelength $\lambda=500$ nm on the mast. What wavelength would be measured and what colour would be observed for this light as seen by a diver submerged in water by the side of the boat? Given $n_w=4/3$.
questions.explanation: Wavelength in water $\lambda_w=\lambda/n_w=500\times3/4=375\approx376$ nm; the colour (determined by frequency, which is unchanged) remains green.

questions.q: The wavelength of the light used in Young's double slit experiment is $\lambda$. The intensity at a point on the screen where the path difference is $\dfrac{\lambda}{6}$ is $I$. If $I_0$ denotes the maximum intensity, then the ratio of $I$ and $I_0$ is .....................
questions.explanation: Phase difference $\delta=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\times\dfrac{\lambda}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. $I/I_0=\cos^2(\delta/2)=\cos^2(30^\circ)=0.75$.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness of a thin film required for constructive interference in the reflected light from it? Given, the refractive index of the film = 1.5, wavelength of the light incident on the film = 600 nm.
questions.explanation: Minimum thickness for constructive interference in reflection: $t=\dfrac{\lambda}{4\mu}=\dfrac{600}{4\times1.5}=100$ nm.

questions.q: Critical angle for certain medium is $\sin^{-1}(0.6)$. The polarizing angle of that medium is .................
questions.explanation: $\sin C=0.6\Rightarrow\mu=1/\sin C=1.6667$. By Brewster's law, $\tan\theta_p=\mu=1.6667$, so $\theta_p=\tan^{-1}(1.6667)$.

questions.q: Red light of wavelength 625 nm is incident normally on an optical diffraction grating with $2\times10^5$ lines/m. Including central principal maxima, how many maxima may be observed on a screen which is far from the grating?
questions.note: At $m=8$, $\sin\theta=1$ (grazing, $\theta=90^\circ$), which many textbooks treat as unobservable, giving a highest usable order of 7 and $2\times7+1=15$ maxima; KEA's key instead counts the 8th order, giving 17.
questions.explanation: Grating spacing $d=1/(2\times10^5)=5000$ nm. $d\sin\theta=m\lambda\Rightarrow m_{max}=d/\lambda=8$, and KEA's key credits this borderline 8th order as observable, giving $2\times8+1=17$ maxima including the central one (as per KEA key).

questions.q: In a given direction, the intensities of the scattered light by a scattering substance for two beams of light are in the ratio of $256:81$. The ratio of the frequency of the first beam to the frequency of the second beam is .....................
questions.explanation:
By Rayleigh's scattering law $I\propto
u^4$, $
u_1/
u_2=(256/81)^{1/4}=4/3$, which does not match any option exactly; KEA awarded grace marks for this question, likely due to this inconsistency.

questions.q: Two luminous point sources separated by a certain distance are at 10 km from an observer. If the aperture of his eye is $2.5\times10^{-3}$ m and the wavelength of light used is 500 nm, the distance of separation between the point sources are just seen to be resolved is
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh's criterion, separation $x=\dfrac{1.22\lambda D}{a}=\dfrac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}\times10^4}{2.5\times10^{-3}}=2.44\ \text{m}$.

questions.q: Young's double slit experiment gives interference fringes of width 0.3 mm. A thin glass plate made of material of refractive index 1.5 is kept in the path of light from one of the slits, then the fringe width becomes
questions.explanation: Inserting a thin plate shifts the fringe pattern but does not change the fringe width, since $\beta=\lambda D/d$ is independent of the plate; so it remains 0.3 mm.

questions.q: Two sources are said to be coherent if they produce waves
options: having same shape of wave front
questions.explanation: Coherent sources emit waves of the same frequency that maintain a constant (time-independent) phase difference.

questions.q: According to Newton's Corpuscular Theory, the speed of light is
questions.explanation: Newton's corpuscular theory predicted that light travels faster in a denser medium (attraction of corpuscles), equivalently it is slower (lesser) in a rarer medium — a prediction later disproved experimentally.

questions.q: For the constructive interference the path difference between the two interfering waves must be equal to
questions.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when the path difference is an integral multiple of the wavelength, $n\lambda$.
